problem: The sentence says a time shift changes only phase 'exactly how a linear filter acts on a periodic input'. A general linear filter multiplies cₙ by H(jnω₀), so it can change both magnitude and phase; a time shift is only the all-pass special case H(jnω₀)=e^{-jnω₀t₀}.
fix: Say: a time shift is the special case that leaves |cₙ| unchanged and adds phase −nω₀t₀; a general linear filter multiplies each cₙ by H(jnω₀), changing both magnitude and phase.

problem: Even symmetry about t=0 does not by itself make even harmonics zero. It makes cₙ real and even (and bₙ=0). Here c₂, c₄, … vanish because the pulse is centered and high for exactly half the period, so sin(nπ/2)=0 for even n.
fix: Replace 'because the pulse is symmetric about t=0' with 'because the pulse is centered and high for exactly half the period, so sin(nπ/2)=0 for even n'.

problem: The scaling statement is wrong for the second mistake. Dropping 1/T₀ scales cₙ by T₀; using 2/T₀ instead of 1/T₀ scales cₙ by 2, not by T₀.
fix: Say: dropping 1/T₀ multiplies every cₙ by T₀; using 2/T₀ instead of 1/T₀ doubles every cₙ.

where: Section 3, integration row of the properties table
problem: The integration property cₙ/(jnω₀) for n≠0 requires x(t) to have zero average (c₀=0). If c₀≠0, ∫x(t)dt contains a ramp and is not periodic, so it has no Fourier series of this form. The text only mentions failure at n=0.
fix: State the condition c₀=0 (zero-mean x(t)); then cₙ/(jnω₀) for n≠0, and the n=0 coefficient is an arbitrary constant. If c₀≠0, the integral is not periodic.

problem: The cosine product formula leaves out n=m=0. For n=m=0 the integral is T₀, not T₀/2. The DC term must be handled separately.
fix: Add: for n=m=0, ∫cos(0)cos(0)dt=T₀; the stated T₀/2 result is for n=m≥1.
